<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" />{{rh|HOLY weeke. 62|THE GOSPEL|CHA. XXII.}}</noinclude>{{verse|chapter=22|verse=1}}{{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=The Gospel vpō the 19 Sunday after Pentecost.}}AND {{sc|Iesvs}} ansvvering, spake againe in parables to them, saying: {{verse|chapter=22|verse=2}}† The kingdom of heauen is likened to a man being a king, vvhich made a ‖ mariage to his sonne. {{verse|chapter=22|verse=3}}† And he sent his ‖ seruants to call them that vvere inuited to the mariage: and they vvould not come. {{verse|chapter=22|verse=4}}† Againe he sent other seruants, saying, Tel them that vvere inuited, Behold I haue prepared my dinner: my beeues and fatlings are killed, and al things are ready: come ye to the mariage. {{verse|chapter=22|verse=5}}† But they neglected: and vvent their vvaies, ‖ one to his farme, and an other to his merchandise: {{verse|chapter=22|verse=6}}† and the rest laid hands vpon his seruants, and spitefully intreating them, murdered them. {{verse|chapter=22|verse=7}}† But vvhen the king had heard of it, he vvas vvroth, and sending his hostes, destroied those murderers, and burnt their citie. {{verse|chapter=22|verse=8}}† Then he saith to his seruants, The mariage in deede is ready: but they that vvere inuited, vvere not vvorthie. {{verse|chapter=22|verse=9}}† Goe ye therfore into the high vvayes: and vvhosoeuer you shal finde, call to the mariage. {{verse|chapter=22|verse=10}}† And his seruants going forth into the vvayes, gathered together al that they found, {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=∷ Not only good men be within the church, but also euil mē. against the Heretikes of these daies.}}∷ bad and good: and the mariage vvas filled vvith ghestes. {{verse|chapter=22|verse=11}}† And the king vvent in to see the ghestes: and he savv there ‖ a man not attired in a vvedding garment. {{verse|chapter=22|verse=12}}† And he saith to him, Frende, hovv camest thou in hither not hauing a vvedding garment? But he vvas dumme. {{verse|chapter=22|verse=13}}† Then the king said to the vvaiters, Binde his hands and feete, and cast him into the vtter darkenes: there shal be vveeping & gnashing of teeth. {{verse|chapter=22|verse=14}}† For many be called, but fevv elect.⊣

{{verse|chapter=22|verse=15}}† {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Mr. 12, 13. Lu. 20, 20.''}}* Then the Pharisees departing, consulted among them selues for to entrappe him in his talke. {{verse|chapter=22|verse=16}}† And they send to him their disciples vvith the Herodians, saying, Maister, vve knovv that thou art a true speaker, and teachest the vvay of God in truth, neither carest thou for any man. for thou doest not respect the person of men: {{verse|chapter=22|verse=17}}† tel vs therfore vvhat is thy opinion, is it lawful to giue tribute to Cæsar, or not? {{verse|chapter=22|verse=18}}† But {{sc|Iesvs}} knovving their naughtines, said, What do you tempt me Hypocrites? {{verse|chapter=22|verse=19}}† Shevv me the tribute coine. And they offred him a penie. {{verse|chapter=22|verse=20}}† And {{sc|Iesvs}} saith to them, Whose is this image and superscription? {{verse|chapter=22|verse=21}}† They say to him, Cæsars. Then he saith to them, Render therfore the things that are Cæsars, ‖ to Cæsar: and the things that are Gods, to God. {{verse|chapter=22|verse=22}}† And hearing it they marueled, and leauing him vvent their vvaies.

{{verse|chapter=22|verse=23}}† {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''* Mr. 12, 18. Lu. 20, 27. Act. 23, 6.''}}* That day there came to him the Sadducees, that say<noinclude>{{rh|||there}}</noinclude>
